label: FI-01 -- a positive control inside the port's region, measured
what_this_is: The RUN, not a description of it. Every number here came out of a command in `commands` below, executed at the commit that added FI-M15 and never re-run selectively. The prediction it scores (`predicted_corpus_port = KILLED`) was committed BEFORE any of it, in `examples/validation/ab/seeded_faults.toml`; the git history carries that ordering.

corpus.note: The region is the GENERATOR'S OWN, printed by `generate cases --port-cases only`, not restated by hand. It is the reason M07 and PA-M14 cannot be decided by any port-scoped instrument: both land on `available` and on a reservation's amount, and neither is in it.

commands.corpus: python3 scripts/tla_spec_dev.py --spec-root specs generate cases examples/validation/ab/model/QuotaLedger.tla examples/validation/ab/model/QuotaLedger.cfg --out <scratch>/specs/corpus-port --package quota_port --view internal --negative-cases with-positive --port-cases only
commands.arm_b: QUOTA_LEDGER_BINDING=rerun_arm_b_binding PYTHONPATH=<measure>:<rerun-measure> python3 <measure>/port_corpus_run.py --cases <scratch>/specs/corpus-port/spec-unit/quota_port --tree <copy of arms/arm_b, clean or with FI-M15 applied> --mapping <measure>/case_adapters.arm-b-port.toml --wiring real

reference_ports.driver: run_port_swap.py (PA-04's, unmodified; one FRESH INTERPRETER per cell)

FI-M15.witness: 384 accepting Commit case(s) executed per corpus column, 388 ran, 0 failed on unmutated code

PA-M14.control_verdict: RED on all four corpus columns, 294 accepting Reserve case(s) executed on each
PA-M14.probe: INERT -- nothing moves after ONE accepted reserve either
PA-M14.note: REPORTED RED, NOT REPAIRED. The probe's INERT verdict and the corpus's four SURVIVED cells are the same fact measured two ways: PA-M14 needs a second action and every generated case runs one.

unchanged_by_this_ticket.note: Reproduced cell for cell against PA-04's and PA-06's sealed tables. FI-01 added a ROW; it moved no cell. Never quote a count from this run against an earlier one without saying so.

arm_b.driver: port_corpus_run.py (the shipped subprocess worker run_port_swap uses), one fresh interpreter per state
arm_b.why_not_run_port_swap: run_port_swap reads arm B's catalogues out of specs/results/, which this epic declares out_of_model and FI-01 does not write. The control is declared in examples/validation/ab/eval/controls_port_region_arm_b.toml and applied to a COPY of the sealed tree; the tree itself is byte-identical afterwards and a test asserts it.

FI-M15.first_failure: case_0014_commit__port_ledger_ledgerappendport: AssertionError: adapter after-state mismatch: committed: expected {'t1': 1, 't2': 0}, actual {'t1': 2, 't2': 0}
FI-M15.note: The failure names `committed`, which is INSIDE the port's declared region. That is the whole claim of this ticket, executed: 384 of 384 accepting Commit cases decide the control.

reference_ports.FI-M15: HOLDS [port-region-commit-path] -- moved: committed, ledger_lines; inside the region: committed, ledger_lines

arm_b.FI-M15: HOLDS [port-region-commit-path] -- moved: available, committed, ledger_lines; inside the region: committed, ledger_lines

what_this_does_NOT_show: It does not show that the port machinery catches anything the hand-written suite does not; FI-M15 is killed by every column including both suites, which is what a control in nobody's gap is supposed to do. It does not retract PA-06-DF-09 -- no generated instrument has a unique kill here either. And it does not make any earlier port-scoped number a count rather than a floor: those runs had no deciding positive control and that is a fact about them, not something this ticket can retroactively repair.
